Text.Text: The annex file is closed. If you still want the Escape Artist lesson, you know where to find me. Keep what you saw downstairs out of idle conversation.
I keep this work for rank 50 in Vibroknife. Get there first. When the job goes wrong, a quiet exit takes more than good intentions.

Six Systemic Shutdown adepts have taken the Veles Militia Annex. They're practicing containment on people who never agreed to the drill. Defeat the six and bring me their ledger. Quietly, if you can. I want the orders before someone loses them.
Take the key to the Militia Annex entrance in the Sheriff and Clinic. Don't let the familiar surroundings make you careless.

A shutdown is useful until it fails. Then you need a way out that doesn't depend on the system cooperating. That's why I teach Escape Artist. The people in the annex have forgotten there's anyone worth getting out with them.
The annex entrance is in the Veles Sheriff and Clinic on Viscara. Take my key there. Anyone coming with you should gather close before you go through.

Six adepts, none of them subtle. They'll telegraph everything - the loud ones always do. That won't make them harmless. Watch the ones who go quiet when you walk in; those learned something real by accident.
Six adepts in the Veles Militia Annex. Bring their drill ledger here to Czerka Tower. Keep the orders intact.
You're back, and nobody followed you. Hand over the ledger.
Names, dates, whose technique came from where. Useful. Six down and nobody official noticed - that's the standard I expect, not the exception.

Five specialists are working the annex range relay. They know how to stop a system and make the failure look ordinary. Beat the five and bring the relay here. I'd like to know which ordinary failures we should worry about.
Back to the annex. Get the relay out before someone has a chance to erase its settings.

The militia doesn't want a scandal, and a scandal is exactly what an unauthorized disabling technique becomes the moment it's loud. Contained quietly, it's a training irregularity. Reported loudly, it's a hearing, a suspension, careers ending over paperwork. I prefer the quiet version. So does everyone above me, whether they admit it or not.
The annex entrance is in the Veles Sheriff and Clinic on Viscara. Take my key there. Anyone coming with you should gather close before you go through.

Five specialists who've stopped telegraphing. They'll try to end the fight before you know it started, which is the whole discipline working as intended, just aimed at you. Don't let them finish a sentence with your name in it.
Five specialists in the annex have the range relay. Beat them and bring it here.
The relay, and you're still unremarked. Hand it over.
Kill logs, timestamps, more than I expected them to keep. Whoever's running this has a warden covering for all of it. That's who's next.
The warden holds the annex. Challenge him there and bring me his scored badge when he's beaten. I'd take someone you trust. Quiet work doesn't have to mean nobody knows where you went.
Arrange your company, then go. I won't ask who. I will ask that they can keep a secret.

He didn't invent Systemic Shutdown, but he's the one who handed it to students who had no clearance for it and no discipline to match. I don't know why yet. I intend to find out from what's left of him.
He answers the challenge marker in the Militia Annex. Your key still gets you inside. Look for your way out before you call him.
He punishes a careless approach quickly. I'd bring help that can notice when you need to get clear. The annex has had enough people disappear into its drills without anyone left to account for them.
Use the annex challenge marker to call the warden. Defeat him and recover the challenge badge.
You're back, and quiet about it. That's the badge, I take it. Hand it over.

Scored and cracked - his record, not yours. He taught more than adepts and specialists. There's an inner circle above him I need accounted for next, and I'd rather account for them before they notice their warden stopped answering.

Four officers still have the captain's chit. They can keep this operation running under militia authority. Defeat the four in the annex and recover it. Then I can start closing the file without leaving the work alive behind it.
Recover the chit. I want the authority closed off as well as the operation.

The drill ledger told me who was being taught. The range relay told me how long it had been going on. The scored badge told me the warden knew it was unauthorized and ran it anyway. Bring me the chit, and I'll know exactly how deep this goes and who signed off on it.
The four officers are inside the Militia Annex. They still have the captain's chit. Recover it, then come back to the tower.
Four of them, and none of them used to working outnumbered. Bring the company you brought last time. I'd rather you finish this with witnesses than alone with a story I have to take on faith.
Four officers in the annex still have the captain's chit. Return it when they're beaten.
That's the chit. Let's see exactly how far this went.
Signatures, authorizations, all of it improvised after the fact to look official. This runs all the way to whoever taught the warden in the first place. One name left on the list.

The master is in the Militia Command Room. Call him at the challenge marker and defeat him. Know your way out before you start. Come back to the tower afterward; we'll see whether this can finally stay finished.
Then go end it. Quietly, if you can manage it. Permanently, either way.

I work alone because one person is easy to account for, easy to disappear if something goes wrong. You're not disposable the same way, and this isn't a job that forgives one mistake. Bring company. Let someone else carry half the risk of what happens down there.
The Militia Command Room. Use the challenge marker there. It's time to find out whether he can finish what he taught the others.

He taught shutdown work before the warden ever learned to spell it. Nobody who went in alone came back to file a report. Bring people who know how to stay quiet about what they see, because they will see something.
The master's challenge marker is in the Militia Command Room. Beat him, get out, and return to Czerka Tower.
You're back, and there's no report to write about him anymore. That's the confirmation I needed.

The shutdown school won't be issuing another order. Your pay is here. You've earned a lesson in Escape Artist, if you want it. We'll start with the route that gets you out when stopping the system doesn't stop the people.
Back to the ledger.
I'll take the first job.
What exactly is a shutdown strike?
Where do I find the annex?
What should I expect from the adepts?
Not yet.
Here's the drill ledger.
Back to the relay.
I'll take the second job.
Why keep this quiet at all?
Where are the specialists working?
What should I expect this time?
Give me time to think it through.
Here's the range relay.
Back to the badge.
I'll bring the company and go.
Who taught the students this in the first place?
Where's the warden's floor?
What should I know about him?
I need to find people I trust first.
Here's the badge.
Back to the chit.
I'll clean house.
What do the recovered items tell you?
Where's the inner circle hiding?
What am I walking into?
Let me finish arranging things.
Here's the chit.
Back to it.
I'll bring people I trust. Let's close this out.
Why send me with company when you work alone?
Where do I find him?
What should I expect from the master?
I need to be sure of who's coming with me.
It's done. He's off the books for good.
